title: Region-aware admission planner and tiered graceful degradation runbook
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Problem: During multi-region incidents and large traffic spikes we observe region-local resource saturation that leads to cascading latency SLO breaches. Current admission control is per-machine and reactive; we need a coordinated, region-aware plan to shed load and degrade gracefully while preserving high-priority customer traffic and avoiding cross-region thrash.

Goal: Design and implement a region-aware admission planner plus a configurable tiered degradation framework that combines priority queuing, admission policies with soft/hard thresholds, circuit breakers per region and model variant, and explicit graceful degradation modes (quality reduction, response truncation, non-streaming fallback, model variant fallback). The system should be observable, configurable per-customer and per-route, and support canary rollout.

Scope: This ticket covers design, core admission controller changes, priority queue metadata propagation, degradation mode enumerations, circuit breaker thresholds and hysteresis, metrics/alerts, runbook and rollout. Integration with Smart Routing and KV cache hints is out-of-scope and will be handled in a follow-up ticket.
implementation_notes:
- Admission planner runs as a region-level controller evaluating regional load profile, SLO burn-rate, and downstream capacity.
- Policies: per-tenant priority weight + SLA tier + route criticality => admission score.
- Admission path: incoming request -> token classifier -> priority bucket -> admission check (soft threshold allows best-effort with degraded mode, hard threshold rejects).
- Queue design: bounded priority queues with preferential headroom for P0/P1 tenants; probabilistic admission for low-priority traffic when soft threshold hit.
- Circuit breakers: expose two circuits per region: latency-burn and error-rate-burn. Breaker states persisted to region-local store with TTL to avoid oscillation. Use exponential backoff for auto-recovery and manual override in Console.
- Degradation modes (ordered): 1) response compression/shorter completions, 2) non-streaming full response truncation, 3) low-cost model variant fallback (quantized or distilled), 4) stub/placeholder response with documentation link. Each mode must be auditable in logs.
- Config: JSON policy per org with priority, weight, allowed degradations, SLO targets. Implement a validation schema and a dry-run flag.
- Backpressure signal endpoints: /admission/v1/status (for routing) and pubsub topic for cross-region notifications.
- Data plane hooks: inject admission metadata header for downstream observability and billing reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Region-level controller deployed to staging serving regions and correctly computes admission decisions against synthetic load.
2) Priority queuing honors tenant weights and preserves P0 traffic under spike tests defined in test harness.
3) Soft-threshold degradation modes execute in order with observable metric changes and annotated logs.
4) Circuit breakers trip and auto-recover with configured hysteresis; manual override from Console reconciles state within 30s.
5) No regressions on latency for non-degraded traffic (latency SLO maintained for P0 routes in canary).
6) Comprehensive runbook created and reviewed by SRE, PM, and Design; alerting and dashboards in place.
7) Feature flags exist for gradual rollout and dry-run validation.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for admission scoring, queue behavior, and degradation transitions.
- Integration tests using local simulator to mimic region failure modes and verify cross-region fallback.
- Chaos tests: kill GPU pool in a region and assert admission controller enforces degradation without global thrash.
- Load testing: replay production traffic traces with skewed tenant distributions and validate P0 preservation and cost metrics.
- A/B canary: roll out to 10% of traffic in staging region and compare SLO burn and error-rate with control group.
- Post-rollback validation: ensure metrics return to baseline after disabling feature flag.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): deploy controller in staging region, dry-run policy for 48h, run synthetic spikes, review metrics.
Phase 2 (canary): enable dry-run->enforce toggle for 5% of production traffic in non-critical region for 72h, collect SLO and error rates.
Phase 3 (regional rollout): increase to 25% then 75% with 24h observation windows; enable Circuit breaker dashboards and pager rules.
Phase 4 (global): enable in all regions with templates for tenants; communicate to customers about potential degradation behaviors and Console controls.
Rollback: feature flag off at region-controller level; circuit breaker persisted state will be cleared after 10m TTL.
Postmortem: any unexpected SLO violation requires incident and postmortem within 72h.
notes: We must coordinate with Console team for manual override controls and with Billing to ensure degraded responses are accounted for. Reach out to Model Onboarding for safe model-variant list. Prioritization: this work is critical for upcoming EU region capacity constraints.
